# Final Review Votes
**Producer:** agent:claude/claude-opus-4-7-max

## Summary

Verified all three amendments against frozenkrill-core/src/secret_sharing.rs and frozenkrill-core/src/wallet_description.rs. Amendment fr-1-14a48673 documents a real metadata-vote denominator-shrinking flaw: dedupe-then-majority lets one tampered share fabricate a strict majority for is_duress and identity once conflicting buckets are dropped, even when threshold reconstruction succeeded from honest distinct ids — this is a legitimate security defect in the new derive_metadata path and should be fixed with regression coverage. Amendment fr-1-b79747ff correctly identifies VssJsonWalletDescriptionV0::from_singlesig as workspace-dead after the split refactor; grep confirms no remaining callers, and proposing a follow-up cleanup bead (or folding into 1si) is sound. Amendment fr-1-bb33648c is a correct informational record: the verification_data/verification_data_hi overwrites at lines 813-814 are never read by any downstream consumer (complete_vsss_share_identifier, derive_metadata, describe_share_group all skip them), and the Vec<owned> SuccessEntry change does broaden the temporal window for cloned secret hex, even though ZeroizeOnDrop keeps it sound.

## Votes

- `fr-1-14a48673`: Accept
  Real denominator-shrinking defect in derive_metadata: tally_source = &deduped, so total_votes and tally_source.len() are computed only over surviving (non-conflicting) buckets. A tampered is_duress=true copy of id 1 plus deliberately conflicting copies of id 2 drops id 2's bucket, leaving id 1 alone and yielding both strict_majority=true and any_duress=true. That promotes attacker-supplied is_duress and identity metadata into the authenticated VssRecovery even though the threshold reconstruction itself used distinct verified ids. Same shape also lets non-complete lo/hi splices remain in the vote for 24-word recoveries because verified_inputs is filtered by per-half wallet_verifies_against_candidate, not by complete_vsss_share_identifier. The proposed fix — restrict the success group to complete verified share ids and treat conflicting-metadata buckets as abstentions counted against the denominator (or fail closed) — is the correct mitigation, and regression tests for duplicate-conflict and lo/hi-splice voting are warranted.
- `fr-1-b79747ff`: Accept
  Dead-code claim verified: workspace grep for `::from_singlesig` and `from_singlesig(` returns only the wallet_description.rs:1356 definition and unrelated `SinglesigPublicMetadataV0::from_singlesig_json` matches; the per-share builder calls in split_singlesig_wallet have been replaced with direct field construction plus original_wallet assignment, leaving the 12-argument constructor with no callers. Removing it shrinks the maintained public API and prevents future callers from re-introducing the verbose constructor. Disposition as a follow-up bead (or folded into the 1si scope which already removes to_singlesig from the same file) is appropriate since the current bead explicitly excludes wallet_description.rs from scope.
- `fr-1-bb33648c`: Accept
  Dead-write observation is correct: after the map closure overwrites verification_data and verification_data_hi (lines 813-814), no downstream consumer reads them — complete_vsss_share_identifier reads share_data/share_data_hi, derive_metadata reads share_data and original_wallet, describe_share_group reads share_index/created_at/threshold/total_shares, and to_recovery's re-call into derive_metadata likewise ignores the rewritten verifier hex. The SuccessEntry shift from Vec<&'a VssJsonWalletDescriptionV0> to Vec<VssJsonWalletDescriptionV0> also genuinely introduces per-candidate clones of hex-encoded secret share material whose lifetime previously matched the borrowed input slice; ZeroizeOnDrop keeps it correct but the duplication window is longer. Worth recording so a future cleanup can either drop the dead overwrites or restore the borrowed-slice form with a SuccessEntry lifetime.
